title: Compact Metric Sparklines: contrast tokens, screenreader announcements & RTL microcopy
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Make the compact metric sparklines and small inline heatmap chips in the Cost Explorer and Rollout Variant Inspector accessible and localization-ready. Deliverables: 1) color-token mapping with explicit contrast targets for every sparkline state (baseline, highlight, muted, delta), 2) keyboard-first focus & selection model for sparkline hover/inspection, 3) screen-reader announcement patterns for dynamic updates and focus changes, 4) microcopy keys and pluralization guidelines for localized metric abbreviations, and 5) RTL layout behavior for collapsed metric rows.

Context: Compact sparklines are used in dense tables and small tiles to show short-term trends. Current implementation relies on subtle low-contrast strokes and hover-only tooltips. That fails WCAG text/icon contrast targets for some tokens and is keyboard-inaccessible. Non-Latin locales expose truncation and abbreviation issues (e.g., localized thousand separators, 'k' vs localized abbreviations). RTL layouts cause label alignment and focus-order regressions in the collapsed row pattern.

Key decisions and trade-offs made in this design:
- Contrast targets: enforce 4.5:1 for any sparkline that conveys a quantitative delta in text-adjacent contexts, and 3:1 for purely decorative mini-graphs when accompanied by a visible text label. We will provide a high-contrast token pair for small stroke widths (1px–1.5px) to meet the effective contrast in real rendering.
- Token strategy: introduce semantic tokens: "metric-sparkline-foreground", "metric-sparkline-muted", "metric-sparkline-alert", and map them to platform color tokens at runtime. This allows runtime overrides for dedicated/high-contrast themes.
- Keyboard model: adopt a roving tabindex pattern for dense metric rows. Tab lands on the row's primary control, arrow keys move focus between inline sparkline segments (for drill-in snapshots), Enter/Space opens the compact inspector panel. This avoids adding additional tab stops for every tiny interactive element.
- Screen reader announcements: use aria-live="polite" on a live region in the compact inspector to announce contextual summaries when focus moves into a sparkline ("Last 24h: rising, +12% with spike at 10:30"). For purely decorative updates during background refresh, rely on visually-hidden status summaries exposed only when the user focuses the row.
- Localization: metric abbreviations will use translation keys (e.g., metrics.abbrev.thousand) rather than hardcoded suffixes. Number formatting will use the Intl API at render-time. For languages with long plurals, ensure the compact inspector allows a longer label line (wrap) and that truncation preserves the first word for identification.
- RTL behavior: flip sparkline start/end so the timeline reads correctly in RTL. Maintain DOM order so screen reader focus order remains logical (label then sparkline then controls). We prefer CSS visual-flip with preserved logical source order to avoid disrupting assistive tech.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- All sparkline visual states pass documented contrast targets on recommended backgrounds (test matrix attached).
- Keyboard navigation covers sparklines: roving tabindex implemented, arrow key navigation documented and demoable in prototype.
- Screen reader announces concise summary when focus enters sparkline; background refreshes do not produce noisy interrupts.
- Localized abbreviations and number formatting validated across 8 languages (en, fr, de, es, pt-BR, ja, ko, ar).
- RTL layout visually mirrors and reading order remains semantic for assistive tech.

Design artifacts and references:
- Figma prototype (compact-sparklines-v3): https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/compact-sparklines-v3
- Prototype demo (keyboard + SR): https://redwood-internal.dev/sandbox/sparklines-proto
- Accessibility test matrix (spreadsheet): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/compact-sparklines-a11y-matrix.xlsx
- Engineering PR placeholder: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-console/pull/xxxx

Open questions / follow-ups for engineering:
- Performance: when sparklines are re-rendered at high-cardinality (2000 rows), we need to evaluate whether additional canvas batching or virtualized DOM segments are required. Engineering to provide perf budget guidance.
- Live region policy: confirm with platform accessibility team whether aria-live polite is preferred vs role=status for our console semantics.
- Token rollout: will runtime token mappings be available to Private installs? If not, agree on a static fallback palette for on-prem customers.

Notes on manual QA and test scripts: see test-cases appended in the attached spreadsheet. QA should run with voiceover, NVDA, and TalkBack on desktop and mobile web, and verify ARIA announcements both on focus and after data refresh. Include tests for number formatting and abbreviation expansion in Spanish and Arabic.
comments: 2026-03-01 - PM Noah Patel: Reviewed scope. Agree with moving forward; please highlight any areas that increase dev effort significantly so we can consider phasing. Noted potential perf risk for large tables.

2026-03-03 - Eng review (Priya Desai): Prefer canvas-based sparklines for perf; will prototype a virtualized rendering approach. Need to confirm fallback for older browsers. Action: ENG-22819 assigned to spike canvas vs SVG.

2026-03-05 - A11y review (Samir Khan): Contrast mapping looks good; recommend increasing muted-state contrast from 2.5:1 to 3:1 for users relying on color to distinguish trend lines. Also suggest explicit focus indicator (1.5x thickness) — update design tokens accordingly.

2026-03-07 - Design update (Ava Martinez): Incorporated Samir's suggestions: muted token raised to target 3:1 and focus stroke increased. Added keyboard interaction diagram to prototype. Updated Figma links.

2026-03-10 - Localization (Mina Chen): Confirmed translation keys for metric abbreviations. Arabic strings reviewed; recommended shorter variant for abbreviations in UI with full expansion in inspector. Added i18n test cases to sheet.

2026-03-12 - QA (Diego Alvarez): Quick pass on Chrome + VoiceOver: live region announcements are working but the phrasing can be shortened to avoid verbosity. Proposed template: "24h trend: up 12%". Updated acceptance criteria to reflect concise SR phrasing.
2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor (assignee): Implementing prototype CSS tokens and roving tabindex demo. Waiting on ENG-22819 perf spike results before finalizing DOM vs canvas recommendation.
acceptance_criteria: Visual contrast meets documented ratios across light/dark/high-contrast themes
Keyboard navigation for sparklines implemented with roving tabindex and arrow-key semantics
Screen reader announces concise summaries only on focus entry; background refreshes do not interrupt
Numbers and abbreviations use i18n keys and Intl formatting for all supported locales
RTL shows mirrored sparkline timeline while preserving DOM reading order
